item.title: - Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the condition why these young bhikkhus, in their prime, with black hair, endowed with the blessing…
item.description:
- Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the condition why these young bhikkhus, in their prime, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the spring of life, do not indulge in sensual desires, but live the holy life completely pure for life, and live the full time perfectly?" - "Great King, the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has said: 'Come, bhikkhus, toward those who are only mothers, establish the mind of a mother. Toward those who are only sisters, establish the mind of a sister. Toward those who are only daughters, establish the mind of a daughter.' Great King, this is the cause, this is the condition why these young bhikkhus... live the holy life completely pure for life, and live the full time perfectly.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.127

item.title: ( Blessed One ): Beautiful parks, Beautiful forests, Beautiful lotus ponds, Are loved by people. They are only worth Little, insignificant. In village or in…
item.description:
( Blessed One ):
Beautiful parks,
Beautiful forests,
Beautiful lotus ponds,
Are loved by people.
They are only worth
Little, insignificant.
In village or in forest,
On low ground or high,
Wherever an Arahant dwells,
That place is truly beautiful.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 11.15

item.title: Elder Gahvaratīriya: In the great forest, bitten by mosquitoes, Like a battle elephant, there one lives mindfully.
item.description:
Elder Gahvaratīriya:

In the great forest, bitten by mosquitoes,
Like a battle elephant, there one lives mindfully.

From: Theragāthā 1.31

item.title: Possessing these ten qualities, bhikkhus, a person should not be associated with. What ten? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false…
item.description:
Possessing these ten qualities, bhikkhus, a person should not be associated with. What ten? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter, covetousness, ill-will, wrong view. Bhikkhus, a person possessing these ten qualities should not be associated with. Possessing these ten qualities, bhikkhus, a person should be associated with. What ten? Abstaining from killing living beings, abstaining from taking what is not given, abstaining from sexual misconduct, abstaining from false speech, abstaining from divisive speech, abstaining from harsh speech, abstaining from idle chatter, non-covetousness, non-ill-will, right view. Bhikkhus, a person possessing these ten qualities should be associated with.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.199

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of peace. What three? Peace of body, peace of speech, and peace of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of peace. What three? Peace of body, peace of speech, and peace of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three kinds of peace.

Peace of body, peace of speech,
Peace of mind, without taints,
One who is perfect in peace,
A sage, is called one who has washed away evil.

From: Itivuttaka 67

item.title: Bhikkhus, if while walking... while standing... while sitting... while lying down, thoughts of sensual desire, or thoughts of ill-will, or thoughts of harming arise in…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, if while walking... while standing... while sitting... while lying down, thoughts of sensual desire, or thoughts of ill-will, or thoughts of harming arise in a bhikkhu, and if he accepts them, does not abandon them, does not dispel them, does not terminate them, does not make them nonexistent — then, bhikkhus, if while lying down, his consciousness behaves thus, he is called one who is not ardent, not conscientious, constantly lazy, of inferior energy.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.11

item.title: Elder Bandhura: I have no need for this or that. I live happily, enjoying the taste of the Dhamma. Having drunk the supreme, first sweetness,…
item.description:
Elder Bandhura:

I have no need for this or that.
I live happily, enjoying the taste of the Dhamma.
Having drunk the supreme, first sweetness,
I will not associate with poison.

From: Theragāthā 1.103

item.title: Rāhula, develop the development like space. Rāhula, by developing like space, agreeable and disagreeable contacts that arise do not take hold of the mind, do…
item.description:
Rāhula, develop the development like space. Rāhula, by developing like space, agreeable and disagreeable contacts that arise do not take hold of the mind, do not remain. Rāhula, just as space is not established anywhere — so too, Rāhula, develop like space. Rāhula, by developing like space, agreeable and disagreeable contacts that arise do not take hold of the mind, do not remain.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 62 – Mahārāhulovādasutta

item.title: Whoever checks the arising anger Like a chariot going straight, I call a charioteer. Others merely hold the reins. Conquer anger by non-anger, Conquer evil…
item.description:
Whoever checks the arising anger
Like a chariot going straight,
I call a charioteer.
Others merely hold the reins.

Conquer anger by non-anger,
Conquer evil by good,
Conquer stinginess by giving,
Conquer falsehood by truth.

Speak the truth, do not be angry,
When asked, give even from little.
By these three conditions,
One may go to the presence of the devas.

The wise do not harm anyone,
Their bodies are always restrained.
They go to the Deathless state,
Where there is no sorrow.

From: Dhammapada 221-234

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, a smith or his apprentice, when looking at his adze handle, sees the marks of his fingers and thumb. He cannot know:…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, a smith or his apprentice, when looking at his adze handle, sees the marks of his fingers and thumb. He cannot know: 'So much of my adze handle wore away today, so much yesterday, so much on other days.' But he knows it is wearing away by the wearing away itself. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is devoted to development does not know: 'So much of my taints wore away today, so much yesterday, so much on other days.' But he knows they are wearing away by the wearing away itself. Just as, bhikkhus, a seafaring ship, fully rigged, stranded for six months due to lack of water in the dry season — its rigging gets damaged by wind and sun, then when the rains come, it becomes weak and rots. So too, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who is devoted to development, the fetters easily weaken and rot.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.101
